entries.message:
QD+LowParse: make Seq-native ITE tag test C-extractable (runtime get_byte callback)

The Seq-native if-then-else tag comparison seqbytes_eq_test read the constant tag
bytes via Seq.index cst (SZ.v j) in its executable loop — Seq.index on a spec
Seq.seq plus the ghost SZ.v is not Low*, so KaRaMeL could not extract the generated
ITE validators/readers (Warning 2: FStar.SizeT.v has no C implementation, on
serverHello_body_test). This path was never exercised: QD unit tests verify ITE
types but never extract them to C.

Fix: seqbytes_eq_test / test_ifthenelse_tag_of_seqbytes_eq now take a C-extractable
get_byte: (j:SZ.t{v j < v clen}) -> (b:byte{b == Seq.index cst (v j)}) callback and
read the constant via it. compile_ite emits <n>_get_byte (an if-chain over j
returning the literal tag bytes, with the impossible fall-through discharged by
<n>_sz_contradiction) and threads it into <n>_test. Generated parser/validator/
reader signatures are unchanged, so downstream consumers need no edits.

entries.subject: 3d: thread EVERPARSE_EXTRA_T through the Pulse extern/static backends
entries.message:
3d: thread EVERPARSE_EXTRA_T through the Pulse extern/static backends

With `--pulse --input_stream extern|static`, the generated
`<Mod>Check<Type>` wrapper kept the Low* signature and still took an
`EVERPARSE_EXTRA_T _extra`, but the parameter stopped there: the Pulse
stream primitives took the stream object alone, so the context reached
only the client's `EverParseHandleError` and `EverParseRetreat`. A client
ported from Low* compiled, linked and ran unchanged while quietly losing
its context.

Thread it, so the generated C matches the Low* contract.

`EverParse3d.InputStream.Base.input_stream_inst` gains a `[@@@no_method]
extra_t: Type0` field, exactly as in the Low* prelude, and its methods
take `(#[solve_from_ctx ()] _extra: extra_t)`. The extern instance sets
it to an assumed `extra_t` (extracted as `EVERPARSE_EXTRA_T`); the buffer
instance sets it to `unit`, which erases completely -- `buffer`'s
generated `EverParse.h` is byte-identical.

Two Pulse-specific obstacles shaped the change:

* a Pulse `fn` drops implicit binders that arrive through a type
  ascription, so the binder cannot live in the `validate_with_action_*`
  or `action` abbreviations; it is declared directly on each `fn`, which
  leaves the arrow types and every validator application site untouched;

* an arrow type stored as a value (`field_ptr_after_t`,
  `field_ptr_after_setter_t`) cannot use a meta-implicit at all, since
  the tactic runs before its binders are in scope. Those two take an
  explicit `_extra` instead.

`EverParse3d.Util.solve_from_ctx` is the Pulse counterpart of the Low*
tactic, with one addition: a `()` fallback, needed because the buffer
instance's `extra_t = unit` reaches the tactic here and does not in Low*.

On the frontend side, `InterpreterTarget.fst` binds the context on every
generated definition under `extern`/`static` (nothing under `buffer`), so
KaRaMeL emits it as the validator's parameter in the same position as
Low*, and `Target.fst` forwards it from the wrapper.

`EverParseStreamGetPosition` is the one primitive that keeps no context:
it is also called from the generated `DefaultErrorHandler`, whose
signature has none. It has no Low* counterpart -- there the position is
ghost -- so no parity is lost.

The `extern` and `static` test clients now check in every primitive that
a sentinel context value arrives intact, so a backend that dropped it
again would fail the suite rather than pass it unnoticed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Port zero_copy_parse combinators to PulseParse

Add zero_copy_parse type and combinators using pts_to_parsed (parser-only)
instead of pts_to_serialized (serializer-based).

LowParse.PulseParse.Base.fst (8 definitions):
- pts_to_parsed_with_perm: analog of pts_to_serialized_with_perm
- zero_copy_parse: type taking parser p instead of serializer s,
  producing vmatch res v with trade back to pts_to_parsed p input
- zero_copy_parse_id: returns input with pts_to_parsed_with_perm
- zero_copy_parse_lens: transforms vmatch via lens
- zero_copy_parse_read: uses PulseParse leaf_reader p
- zero_copy_parse_ignore: ignores parsed value
- zero_copy_parse_ext: parser extensionality
- zero_copy_parse_ifthenelse: conditional dispatch

LowParse.PulseParse.Combinators.fst (5 definitions):
- zero_copy_parse_synth: for parse_synth
- zero_copy_parse_filter: for parse_filter
- zero_copy_parse_nondep_then: pairs two parsers, uses jumper for p1
  to compute split point (replaces serializer-based split)
- zero_copy_parse_dtuple2: dependent pair, uses jumper
- read_and_zero_copy_parse_dtuple2: reads first, zero-copy second

Key differences from serializer-based versions:
- Permission halving: pts_to_parsed_intro gives pm /. 2.0R
- Jumpers replace serializer-computed split points
- No serializer dependency in types

No admit() or assume. Verified with make lowparse.

entries.subject: Replace ParserStrong with parser_kind_injective in gaccessor
entries.message:
Replace ParserStrong with parser_kind_injective in gaccessor

Replace the overly restrictive k2.parser_kind_subkind == Some ParserStrong
precondition on gaccessor_compose and related functions with the weaker
k2.parser_kind_injective == true. This restores the previous expressivity
of gaccessors in LowParse.Low.

Key changes:
- Add gaccessor_injective back to gaccessor_prop' (conjunction with
  gaccessor_no_lookahead), so gaccessor constructors must prove both
- Change gaccessor_compose, gaccessor_compose_eq, accessor_compose to
  require k2.parser_kind_injective == true instead of ParserStrong
- Add gaccessor_compose_injective proof (uses injective_precond +
  no_lookahead of intermediate parser p2)
- Update gaccessor_compose_no_lookahead proof to use injective_precond
- Change gaccessor_fst_then, gaccessor_then_fst, gaccessor_then_snd and
  their accessor variants to use parser_kind_injective == true
- Add gaccessor_snd_injective call to gaccessor_snd construction
- Add _injective lemma calls to gaccessor constructions in:
  LowParse.Low.Combinators (tagged_union_payload)
  LowParse.Low.Sum (sum_payload, dsum_payload, dsum_unknown_payload)
  LowParse.Low.IfThenElse (ifthenelse_payload)
  LowParse.Low.VLGen (bounded_vlgen_payload, vlgen_payload)
- Add parser_kind_injective == true to LowParse.Repr.fsti strong_parser_kind

entries.subject: CBOR: switch cbor_raw_sort to depth-measured sort_t / sort_aux_t
entries.message:
CBOR: switch cbor_raw_sort to depth-measured sort_t / sort_aux_t

The rebased Pulse merge-sort library (Pulse.Lib.Sort.Merge.Slice) now
parameterizes sort_aux_t/sort_t by a ghost measure n: Ghost.erased nat
(bounding the slice length) and takes the recursive worker as a bounded
closure (m: Ghost.erased nat { m << n }) -> sort_aux_t ... m, so the
recursion carries an explicit decreasing argument (F* PR 4358).

Update cbor_raw_sort_aux to the new type: add the ghost n parameter and
the pure (SZ.v (S.len a) <= n) precondition, pass n and the bounded
closure (fun m -> cbor_raw_sort_aux p m) to Slice.sort_aux, and add
decreases (Ghost.reveal n). Thread n through cbor_raw_sort and seed it
at the single call site with SZ.v (S.len a) (trivially satisfying the
bound). n is fully ghost, so C/Rust extraction is unchanged.

Verified with make -j16 cbor-verify.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

entries.message:
qd -pulse: emit size_<n> surface + wire bcvli vlgen-list write_<n>

Phase 3d generator wiring for Layer 3 (variable-width length headers).

- Add a parallel copyful safe-SIZE emission axis (l2r_safe_size / size_<n>):
  copyful_sizes registry + register_size/size_registered/copyful_size_available/
  copyful_size_name, is_copyful_safe_size_leaf_type + safe_leaf_size_expr
  (constant-size leaf sizes via PPB.l2r_safe_size_leaf), mirroring the writer
  registry exactly. size_<n> is gated on all field/element sizes being available.
- Emit size_<n> in: emit_copyful_safe_leaf_writer (enums/const sums), the struct
  emitter (pair-tree via PPC.l2r_safe_size_pair + l2r_safe_size_synth), and
  emit_copyful_bytes via a new optional ?size arg (flbytes/bounded_vlbytes/
  bounded_vlbytes' -> PPBY.l2r_safe_size_*).
- Wire vllist write_<n> (emit_copyful_vllist) via
  PPVG.l2r_safe_writer_bounded_vlgen_payload with a bcvli header
  (PPBCVLI.bounded_bcvli_size / l2r_leaf_write_bounded_bcvli) + the element
  list writer/size (PPLS.l2r_safe_writer_list / l2r_safe_size_list), synth-lifted.
  Gated on lenty=bitcoin_varint and the element type having both writer+size.
  Large size bounds (>= 65536) emitted via FStar.SizeT.uint_to_t under
  fits_u64_implies_fits (SizeT literals are capped at 65535).

Verified T31-T34 individually + full make -j16 quackyducky-pulse-test GREEN
(verify + extract-to-C + link + run), no admits.

Add validate_dsum_cases_fn/jump_dsum_cases_fn generic combinators

produce a validator/jumper for parse_dsum_cases, using

fn equivalents of validate_dsum_cases/jump_dsum_cases, ensuring ref
operations are properly lowered for extraction.

  calls parse_dsum_cases_eq' for the proof, dispatches via
  validate_dsum_cases_dispatch with repr_of_maybe_enum_key
- jump_dsum_cases_fn: same pattern for jumpers

Update Example9 to use the generic combinators:
- Pre-compute tactic destructors as let bindings (outside fn)
- validate_t/jump_t call PPS.validate_dsum_cases_fn/jump_dsum_cases_fn

entries.subject: LowParse: read little-endian UINT16 directly into U16.t
entries.message:
LowParse: read little-endian UINT16 directly into U16.t

read_u16_le went through read_bounded_integer_le_2, whose result type is
bounded_integer 2 (a U32.t subtype), and then narrowed back via synth_u16_le
(uint32_to_uint16). This widen-then-narrow round-trip produced redundant
(uint16_t)(uint32_t) casts in extracted C for every little-endian UINT16 read.

Read the value directly into U16.t with make_total_constant_size_reader over
load16_le_i, coerced to parse_u16_le with leaf_reader_ext, mirroring the
big-endian read_u16 and the native read_u64_le. No spec or interface change;
only the reader implementation is affected, so both 3D (read____UINT16) and
quackyducky (LL.read_u16_le) benefit.

entries.subject: 3d: qualify the library names the Pulse state dictionary is built from
entries.message:
3d: qualify the library names the Pulse state dictionary is built from

A 3D parameter is printed as a plain F* binder carrying the user's own
name, and the generated Pulse module opens EverParse3d.State and
Pulse.Lib.Pervasives. InterpreterTarget printed the state dictionary
using six of those opened names unqualified -- state_dict,
state_dict_empty, state_dict_singleton, state_dict_prod,
state_dict_weaken_prop and pts_to -- so a parameter with any of those
names shadowed the library definition and the generated code did not
typecheck. The Low* backend has neither the opens nor the state
dictionary and accepted the same grammars, e.g.

  entrypoint
  typedef struct _E1 (UINT32 state_dict_empty) {
    UINT8 a { a == state_dict_empty };
  } E1;

which failed with "Expected expression of type
EverParse3d.State.state_dict, got expression state_dict_empty".

The comment above pulse_output_state_key argues that a compiler-owned
name cannot be shadowed because it starts with Ast.reserved_prefix. That
is true of the definitions it introduces, but says nothing about library
names reached through an open; extend it to say so.

Print those names fully qualified, as A.copy_buffer_state_dict on the
next line already was. Fully qualified rather than through a new module
abbreviation, so that nothing new is added to the generated module
prefix. Pulse.Lib.Pervasives includes Pulse.Class.PtsTo after
Pulse.Lib.Reference, so Pulse.Class.PtsTo.pts_to is exactly what the
bare name already resolved to and the qualification is inert.

Add ReservedNames.3d to both src/3d/tests and share/everparse/tests/3d,
where the non-FAIL *.3d wildcard picks it up automatically for the Low*
and Pulse batteries and for pulse-diff. It uses all six names as
parameters: mutable ones, which become dictionary leaves; plain ones,
which only appear in refinements; and a non-entrypoint type, where the
names appear in the dtyp_ signature rather than in a dictionary.
pulse-diff goes from 64874 to 67128 top-level cases, 1846 of them
ReservedNames, all identical between the two backends.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Generate copyful parsers for leaf-readable closed sums; export struct/sum copyful via .fsti

A fully leaf-readable closed sum (all payloads flat / by-value) gets a copyful
parser that copies the whole value out of the input into a fresh, owned value
(vmatch = pure equality, free = no-op), reusing the existing leaf reader.

Also introduce a uniform copyful low-representation type (<n>_lowtype) and
export struct and sum copyful combinators (<n>_vmatch / read_<n> / free_<n>)
through the .fsti so composite types can reuse them across modules.

entries.subject: 3d/pulse: make extern field positions relative to the validation origin
entries.message:
3d/pulse: make extern field positions relative to the validation origin

`EverParse3d.InputStream.Extern`'s `get_position` returned the stream's
*cumulative* position, so re-validating on the same stream object made
`field_pos_64` (and the default error handler) report offsets that kept
growing across successive top-level validations. Low* threads an explicit
position pair and its wrapper always passes a start position of 0, so the
two backends disagreed.

Give the extern/static backend's `pos_t` a runtime value: the *origin*,
i.e. the absolute stream position at which the current top-level
validation began. `input_stream_inst` already threads `sl_pos` unchanged
through every combinator and nested type call, so enclosing-relative
offsets at ordinary nested calls are preserved and
`EverParse3d.Actions.Base` needs no change at all.

  - `stream_pts_to base len origin contents v` now means "the stream
    consumed `origin` bytes before `contents` began".
  - The assumed `stream_get_position` keeps its C name and is respecified
    as absolute; a new derived `stream_get_relative_position` subtracts
    the origin and is what the instance exposes as `get_position`.
  - Every other assumed val takes the origin as `Ghost.erased`, so the
    C prototypes the client implements are unchanged. Only the generated
    validators and the generated error handler gain one `size_t`.
  - `stream_trunc_pos` returns the origin unchanged, consistent with
    `stream_truncate`, whose postcondition already continues the parent's
    position accounting.

As a bonus this also aligns the extern error callback with Low*: it now
reports `EverParseStreamGetPosition(base) - origin` rather than the raw
cumulative position, closing a previously acknowledged divergence.

The buffer backend is unaffected (its `pos_t` is already a `ref SZ.t`
that the wrapper initializes to 0).

Adds a FIELDPOS regression entrypoint to the extern test, which validates
the same stream twice and checks that both runs report offset 0.

entries.subject: EverCDDL/roundtrip: delegate F* to common.Makefile via extract.Makefile
entries.message:
EverCDDL/roundtrip: delegate F* to common.Makefile via extract.Makefile

The hand-rolled F* invocations in src/cddl/tests/roundtrip/Makefile
(one for typecheck, one for OCaml extraction, with explicit
--include / --cache_dir / --odir / --already_cached / --cmi flags)
have been replaced with a single recursive invocation of a small
auxiliary Makefile, extract.Makefile, that includes the standard
EverParse common.Makefile and lets it drive F*.

extract.Makefile is parameterised by two command-line variables:
  MNAME            -- the F* module name (RoundtripDpe, ...).
  OUTPUT_DIRECTORY -- the per-target sandbox (_output/dpe, ...).
It sets FSTAR_FILES, CACHE_DIRECTORY, ALREADY_CACHED and
FSTAR_DEP_OPTIONS for that single module, and exposes an 'extract'
goal that asks common.Makefile for $(ALL_ML_FILES). common.Makefile
then handles dependency discovery (.depend), typechecking
(.fst.checked) and OCaml extraction (.ml), so each F* invocation
uses the same options as the rest of EverParse.

The outer Makefile's per-target template now contains a single rule:

    _output/T/<MNAME>.ml: _output/T/<MNAME>.fst extract.Makefile
        +$(MAKE) -f extract.Makefile MNAME=<MNAME> OUTPUT_DIRECTORY=_output/T

Each target's recursive make sees a distinct OUTPUT_DIRECTORY and
FSTAR_DEP_FILE, so make -j over the three targets is still safe.

Bonus side-effect: incremental rebuilds are now properly no-ops
($(GEN), $(CDDLS) and the auxiliary Makefile are unchanged, so the
.ml is up to date and the recursive make is never invoked); the only
remaining work is the .PHONY check.exe runs. A clean parallel run
still takes ~4.5s on this host (five back-to-back stress runs all
pass with three Check: OK).

entries.subject: rewrite the CDDL syntax parser to determine typ vs. group names after the fact
entries.message:
rewrite the CDDL syntax parser to determine typ vs. group names after the fact

from RFC 8610 Appendix C:

   Note that whether the name
   defined by a rule stands for a type or a group isn't always
   determined by syntax alone: e.g., "a = b" can make "a" a type if "b"
   is a type, or a group if "b" is a group.  More subtly, in "a = (b)",
   "a" may be used as a type if "b" is a type, or as a group both when
   "b" is a group and when "b" is a type (a good convention to make the
   latter case stand out to the human reader is to write "a = (b,)").
   (Note that the same dual meaning of parentheses applies within an
   expression but often can be resolved by the context of the
   parenthesized expression.  On the more general point, it may not be
   clear immediately either whether "b" stands for a group or a type --
   this semantic processing may need to span several levels of rule
   definitions before a determination can be made.)

entries.subject: 3d/pulse: fix the size_t static assertion direction
entries.message:
3d/pulse: fix the size_t static assertion direction

The Pulse backend emitted two _Static_asserts in the generated wrapper:

  sizeof(size_t) >= sizeof(uint32_t)
  sizeof(size_t) >= sizeof(uint64_t)

The first is load-bearing: it backs EverParse3d.Actions.Base.size_t_fits_u32,
an `assume val` of FStar.SizeT.fits_u32, which justifies every uint32_t ->
size_t widening (the wrapper's `len`, and the `n` of validate_nlist,
validate_t_at_most and validate_t_exact). C only guarantees SIZE_MAX >= 65535,
so it has to be asserted.

The second was backwards. Nothing in lib/everparse/3d converts a uint64_t to a
size_t: there is no `fits_u64` assumption and no use of SZ.uint64_to_sizet, and
probe offsets and sizes stay uint64_t end to end, exactly as in Low*. What the
code does do is the opposite, size_t -> uint64_t, via the truncating
SZ.sizet_to_uint64: the field_pos_64 action, the field_ptr_after bounds check,
the position handed to the error callback, and the extern wrapper's
size_t -> uint64_t -> size_t round trip of the validation origin. Ruling that
truncation out needs an upper bound on size_t, not a lower one.

As written the assertion was also the sole blocker for 32-bit Pulse builds,
which Low* supports: at -m32, Demo0Wrapper.c failed the assertion while
Demo0.c compiled fine. With the direction flipped, all 50 generated validators
and wrappers compile at both -m32 and -m64.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

entries.subject: Refactor copyful_parse to t_mid/conv design in src/lowparse/pulse
entries.message:
Refactor copyful_parse to t_mid/conv design in src/lowparse/pulse

Change the copyful parser type from
  copyful_parse (vmatch: t'->t->slprop) p
to
  copyful_parse (vmatch: t'->tm->slprop) p (conv: tm -> GTot (option t))
with postcondition vmatch_conv vmatch conv res v, so all refinements on the
high-level value type are moved into the partial conv and the vmatch RHS type
tm is refinement-free. This enables future gracefully-failing serializers
(esp. vldata/fldata size constraints, container counts).

Converted modules: Base (vmatch_conv/intro/elim/free_vmatch_conv + leaf/synth/
ext), Combinators (synth/pair), VLData/FLData/VLGen (size conv), Bytes,
Array/VCList/List (packed-high element relation + count conv), Sum (sum/dsum/
sum_cases with sum-level identity conv, per-case field relations packed via
vmatch_conv).

entries.subject: 3d: honor --init_locals and --hoist_locals in generated C files
entries.message:
3d: honor --init_locals and --hoist_locals in generated C files

The --init_locals and --hoist_locals options were only being passed to
KaRaMeL for F*-extracted C code. The C files directly generated by 3d
(notably *Wrapper.c) were not honoring these options.

With --init_locals, uninitialized local variable declarations now get
zero initializers: = { 0 } for structs (c99/c89), = { } (c23), and
= 0 for scalars/pointers.

With --hoist_locals, all local variable declarations are hoisted to
the top of each function body, with initializers separated into
assignment statements.

When both options are used together, hoisted declarations get zero
initializers.

entries.subject: 3d/pulse: extract and compile all Pulse 3d tests
entries.message:
3d/pulse: extract and compile all Pulse 3d tests

Removes the last KaRaMeL extraction blockers for the --pulse backend, so
that every test in share/everparse/tests/3d now goes all the way to C.
The exclusion list is gone and 61 C files compile (previously 40).

Runtime fixes:

- Actions.Base: probe_then_validate bound the pure external address
  conversion as `let a64 = as_u64 src` and applied it separately. That
  partial application of an extern cannot be closed over in C. Apply it
  fully, as validate_with_probe already did.

- action_field_ptr, action_field_ptr_after and
  action_field_ptr_after_with_setter now take the operation directly
  instead of an option plus a squash witness, and the interpreter does
  the Some?.v projection. Building the option at runtime forced KaRaMeL
  to keep a function type with unit arguments inside a data constructor,
  whose arity no longer matched after unused-parameter elimination.
  Since Some?.v is already in specialization_steps, the projection is
  discharged by the normalizer, provided the backend definitions unfold:
  hence the new specialize_backend attribute in Actions.Common, which
  the backends can reference without depending on the interpreter.

C plumbing:

- Under --pulse the copy buffer is a concrete struct emitted into
  EverParse.h, which clashed with the legacy `typedef void*
  EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T` of EverParseEndianness.h. That typedef is now
  guarded, and --pulse code includes the new EverParsePulseEndianness.h,
  which defines the guard before delegating. Pulse wrapper headers also
  include EverParse.h so that the struct is in scope.

entries.subject: Pulse l2r_safe_writer: leaf, coerce_mid, and pair combinators
entries.message:
Pulse l2r_safe_writer: leaf, coerce_mid, and pair combinators

Begin Phase 1 of gracefully-failing serializer (l2r_safe_writer) support.
Add three foundational combinators, all verified:

- l2r_safe_writer_leaf (Base.fst): the copyful leaf representation is the
  value (eq_as_slprop) and leaf_conv never fails, so the writer fails only
  when there is no room. Constant-size leaf so the serialized size is known
  before writing; checks room then delegates to the low-level l2r_leaf_writer.
- l2r_safe_writer_coerce_mid (Base.fst): re-index a writer from an inner mid
  type to an exposed mid type, mirroring free_coerce_mid on the predicate and
  additionally matching conv pointwise. Reuses the same per-type bridge lemmas
  generated for read_<n>.

entries.subject: 3d --pulse: make EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T work on every input stream
entries.message:
3d --pulse: make EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T work on every input stream

Under --pulse, EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T was printed as `B.copy_buffer_t`,
where `B` is the input-stream module alias. Only the buffer backend defines
that name: EverParse3d.InputStream.Buffer re-exports the four
EverParse3d.CopyBuffer.Buffer names, while the Extern and Static instances
do not.

So any .3d file that merely mentions EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T -- as a type
parameter, or as the parameter of an extern action -- was accepted by the
frontend under --input_stream extern/static and then rejected by F* on the
generated code with

  Error 72: Identifier copy_buffer_t not found in module B

The Low* backend compiles the same grammar on every input stream, since
there the copy buffer is a single stream-independent abstract type.

The buffer-only guard that exists for probes
(InterpreterTarget.fst, T_probe_then_validate) does not cover this: a
grammar can use a copy buffer without probing at all.

Print the type by its defining module instead, EverParse3d.CopyBuffer.Buffer,
which is already assumed abstract and independent of any input stream. The
generated public API is then identical to the one Low* produces, e.g.

  uint64_t ModCheckP(EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T dest, EVERPARSE_EXTRA_T _extra,
                     EVERPARSE_INPUT_STREAM_BASE base);

Probing itself stays buffer-only: the probe monad's instance arguments
(Target.fst, InterpreterTarget.fst) still reach input_stream_buffer and
copy_buffer_buffer through `B`, and lifting that is a separate change.

Add share/everparse/tests/3d/copy_buffer_backend, which pins both halves:
Test.3d must build on buffer, extern and static -- with --batch, since the
regression was invisible to the frontend -- and Probe.3d must still be
rejected on extern and static.

Document the probe restriction in sec-probing-pulse, whose opening sentence
claimed that everything about probing carries over to --pulse unchanged.

entries.subject: Pulse copyful sums: refinement-free mids + tight conv (option b)
entries.message:
Pulse copyful sums: refinement-free mids + tight conv (option b)

Rewrite the closed-sum, open/dsum, and implicit-sum copyful_parse
generators and the supporting LowParse.PulseParse.Sum / Base library
combinators so each sum's separation-logic predicate (vmatch) uses a
refinement-free per-tag "mid" type and a tight partial conversion
conv (Some iff representable), pushing all refinements into conv.

This is the prerequisite for gracefully-failing l2r_safe_writer
serializers: with refinement-free mids, a serializer can attempt to
write and fail at runtime rather than requiring a proof that all
refinements hold up front.

Library (src/lowparse/pulse):
- Base.fst: add copyful_parse_coerce_mid / free_coerce_mid value-level
  re-indexing combinators (retype the vmatch RHS / conv between an
  inner mid and an exposed mid via a squashed extensionality witness);
  named leaf_conv.
- Sum.fst: closed/open/implicit copyful sections reworked to the new
  mid_of_tag / conv_of_tag tight-conv API (sum_cases_conv,
  vmatch_sum_cases, copyful_parse_sum_cases, free_sum_cases, etc.).

Generator (src/qd/rfc_fstar_compiler.ml):
- emit_copyful_owned_sum / _owned_dsum / _implicit_sum emit a
  transparent refinement-free <n>_mid(_of_tag), a transparent tight
  <n>_conv(_of_tag), identity-retype bridges, and norm;trefl
  extensional-equality bridge lemmas, then build read_<n>/free_<n>
  via copyful_parse_coerce_mid / free_coerce_mid.
- Implicit sums cross a propositional (not definitional) boundary
  between t19 k and sum_cases t19_sum (as_enum_key k); the conv bridge
  lemma is discharged by norm then SMT (which erases the refinement)
  rather than trefl, with the per-tag <n>_eq_lemma in scope.

Verified green end-to-end via make -j16 quackyducky-pulse-test
(237 modules verified, extract-to-C + run), no admits.

QuackyDucky/LowParse Pulse: read_sum_tag via the [@Norm] enum destructor

read_sum_tag computed the sum (closed-key) tag by applying the spec list-walker
enum_key_of_repr (sum_enum t) k' directly, leaking runtime F* cons-list traversals
(list_map flip + L.assoc) into the extracted C for every sum/select dispatch
(e.g. Handshake, ServerName).

the key via the reducible [@Norm] dependent destructor (reusing read_enum_key_t/_f
/_eq/_if), keeping enum_key_of_repr in ghost position; bridge with the
maybe_enum_key_of_repr_known lemma.  Thread a dep_maybe_enum_destr_t (sum_enum t)
(read_enum_key_t (sum_enum t)) tag destructor through read_sum_tag, read_sum and
copyful_parse_sum, and have QuackyDucky supply it via
(_ by (LP.dep_maybe_enum_destr_t_tac ())) at the read_<n>_sum emission sites.

Verified; re-extracting the agentic-tls TLS parsers removes ALL forward enum
list-walkers (enum_key_of_repr / maybe_enum_key_of_repr / list_mem / list_map) from
the C.

chained after EverParseEndianness.h so a parallel make never runs the
micro-step concurrently, make them prerequisites of EverParse.h, and add
them to EVERPARSE_ALL_H_FILES.

EverParse.h / EverParseEndianness.h, so they are treated like every other
file the tool copies into the output directory.

entries.subject: 3d: let a 3D module be named I under --pulse
entries.message:
3d: let a 3D module be named I under --pulse

EverParse3d.ProbeActions.fst refers to I.input_stream_inst while taking
the I abbreviation from its own .fsti, rather than declaring one. An
abbreviation that only leaks from the interface is invisible to F*'s
dependency analysis, which therefore resolves I. against a client module
literally named I:

  EverParse3d.InputStream.Buffer.fst
    `uses` EverParse3d.Actions.Base.fsti
    `uses` EverParse3d.ProbeActions.fst
    `uses` <odir>/I.fsti

so a grammar as small as

  entrypoint typedef struct _I { UINT32 a; } I;

failed with "Error 308: Recursive dependency on module I.fsti", while the
Low* backend accepted it. The Low* prelude never hits this because every
file there that uses I. declares the abbreviation itself; that is exactly
the asymmetry. Declare it in ProbeActions.fst too.

Separately, drop `module I = EverParse3d.InputStream.Base` from the Pulse
module prefix emitted by Main.fst. Each abbreviation there shadows a 3D
module of the same name inside every generated file, and this one is
unused: across the 355 generated .fst/.fsti in the test corpus nothing
refers to EverParse3d.InputStream.Base. That is hygiene, not the fix --
re-injecting the abbreviation into the generated I.fst/I.fsti after the
ProbeActions change still typechecks.

B is deliberately untouched. It is genuinely used (B.base_t,
B.field_ptr, B.error_handler_macro, ...), and it is the Low* backend that
rejects a 3D module named B, for a pre-existing reason in its own
prelude.

Add I.3d to src/3d/tests and share/everparse/tests/3d, where the
non-FAIL *.3d wildcard picks it up for both batteries and for pulse-diff,
which goes from 67128 to 67568 top-level cases with the I traces
identical between the backends.

entries.subject: Add constraint for UDP's length field
entries.message:
Add constraint for UDP's length field

https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc768.txt

> Length  is the length  in octets  of this user datagram  including  this header  and the data.   (This  means  the minimum value of the length is eight.)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_Datagram_Protocol#UDP_datagram_structure

> This field specifies the length in bytes of the UDP header and UDP data. The minimum length is 8 bytes, the length of the header. The field size sets a theoretical limit of 65,535 bytes (8-byte header + 65,527 bytes of data) for a UDP datagram. However, the actual limit for the data length, which is imposed by the underlying [IPv4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPv4) protocol, is 65,507 bytes (65,535 bytes − 8-byte UDP header − 20-byte [IP header](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPv4_header)).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_Datagram_Protocol#cite_note-5)
Using IPv6 [jumbograms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumbogram) it is possible to have UDP datagrams of size greater than 65,535 bytes. The length field is set to zero if the length of the UDP header plus UDP data is greater than 65,535.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_Datagram_Protocol#cite_note-rfc2675-6)

3d/pulse-diff: cover ActAndCheck.3d and FieldDependence0.3d

pulse-diff read src/3d/tests/out.batch and share/everparse/tests/3d/out.pulse,
which are built from `positive_tests`. That variable filters out
ActAndCheck.3d and FieldDependence0.3d, so neither was ever compared between
the two backends.

The exclusion is a leftover. It dates from commit 7b2764b70, which introduced
both ActAndCheck.3d and the :act/:check actions, back when 3D had two
translation backends and --interpret chose between them: batch-test drove
Translate.fst, batch-interpret-test drove TranslateForInterpreter.fst, and
those two files were only supported by the latter. Translate.fst and
--interpret are both long gone, so batch-test and batch-interpret-test now
drive an identical pipeline and differ only in which files they feed it --
`positive_tests` versus `INTERPRETABLE_FILES`, i.e. every non-FAIL .3d.

So point the harness at the batch-interpret outputs instead. Both backends
already generate identical wrapper signatures for the two files, and both
entrypoints take the buffer ABI, so they need no other change. This is worth
doing: ActAndCheck.3d is the only test exercising :act/:check, and one of just
three using field_pos.

Top-level comparison goes from 42 to 47 entrypoints; 64874 cases, Low* and
Pulse identical.

unchanged for Low*, for all three backends and for both gmake and nmake;
and EverParse.h + EverParsePulse.h together compile cleanly from the new
path for buffer, extern and static, where the old path failed.

entries.subject: 3d: key state_dict entries by parameter, not by formal name
entries.message:
3d: key state_dict entries by parameter, not by formal name

A copy buffer, or an output pointer, that a type receives as a parameter
cannot be keyed in its state_dict by a literal derived from the name of that
parameter. The same buffer reaches different types under different parameter
names, and two keys for one resource defeat the purpose of the keys.
Specialize6 hit exactly this: RESP baked "___ResponseProbe" while its caller
passed ___HeadersProbe.

So every generated definition now takes one erased key per parameter, and a
leaf that is a parameter is keyed by that erased string. Callers forward
their own key for a parameter they pass on, and Ghost.hide of a literal for
anything else. A definition whose dictionary is a product also takes the
pairwise key disequalities it needs, since those are no longer decidable by
normalization; its callers discharge them from their own.

Keys are therefore ghost, so the key arguments of the action and probe
combinators become Ghost.erased string: they are used only in types, and
validate_X shares the binders of def_X.

Also drop the delta_attr [%specialize] normalization from the by-clause of
def_X under --pulse. It is what made the SMT encoding of FineGrainedProbe-
Specialize and Specialize6 blow up (20 GB of F* heap, Z3 never spawned), and
unlike the Low* backend, whose inv/eloc/disj indices it computes, the Pulse
backend passes the state_dict explicitly and does not need it.

Both tests now verify, so neither is excluded any more: all 25 positive and
all 10 negative tests of share/everparse/tests/3d pass.

entries.message:
EverCDDL: downgrade evercddl-lib from fstar.pluginlib to fstar.lib

With the F* plugin gone, evercddl-lib no longer needs the full F*
compiler at runtime; the slim fstar.lib runtime suffices. This drops
the fstar.compiler transitive dependency (dynlink, sedlex, menhirLib,
mtime, ppxlib-for-compiler, batteries, compiler-libs, ...) from the
extracted OCaml library.

Three changes wired together:

  * Drop the [@@plugin] attribute from literal/elem_typ/group/decl in
    CDDL.Spec.AST.Base. With no in-tree consumer of the generated
    embeddings, this purely suppresses the __knot_e_* code path in
    extraction (it has no effect on F* verification).

  * Drop `FSTAR_ML_CODEGEN := Plugin` in src/cddl/tool/ocaml.Makefile.
    Extraction now uses the default --codegen OCaml from
    src/common.Makefile, producing bare Prims.* / FStar_*.* calls
    instead of the Fstarcompiler.*-prefixed plugin form.

  * In src/cddl/tool/ocaml/evercddl-lib/dune, swap fstar.pluginlib for
    fstar.lib in (libraries ...). The fstar.lib package is unwrapped
    (modules are top-level FStar_*, Prims, Stdint) so the
    `open Fstar_pluginlib` lines in the handwritten CDDLLexer.mll,
    CDDLParser.ml and Tokens.ml are no longer needed and are removed.

Verified by make -j16 cddl (clean rebuild) and make -j16 cddl-test
cose-test (both pass).

entries.subject: QD + LowParse: emit bytesize_eqn for if-then-else types
entries.message:
QD + LowParse: emit bytesize_eqn for if-then-else types

An if-then-else serializes as tag ++ payload (LP.serialize_ifthenelse =
bare_serialize_ifthenelse = Seq.append (serialize tag) (serialize payload)), so
its bytesize is the constant discriminant length plus the payload bytesize.
Previously QuackyDucky emitted only the opaque <n>_bytesize_eq for ite types,
with no [SMTPat] decomposition — unlike structs/sums — so an enclosing struct's
bytesize_eqn (and downstream length lemmas like agentic-tls's
lemma_serialize_server_hello_len) could not decompose an ite field automatically.

- LowParse.Spec.IfThenElse.fst (no .fsti — transparent): add
  length_serialize_ifthenelse, exposing
    Seq.length (serialize (serialize_ifthenelse s) x)
    == Seq.length (serialize tag_ser t) + Seq.length (serialize payload_ser y)
  where (| t, y |) = serialize_ifthenelse_synth_recip x. Proved from
  bare_serialize_ifthenelse + Seq.lemma_len_append.
- rfc_fstar_compiler.ml (compile_ite, after write_bytesize): emit per-constructor
  SMTPat lemmas <n>_bytesize_eqn_<true_ctor> / _<false_ctor>
    <n>_bytesize (<ctor> ·) == clen + <payload>_bytesize ·
  (per-constructor because the two arms have distinct payload types), mirroring
  the sum path's per-case bytesize_eqn. Discharged via length_serialize_ifthenelse,
  the constant tag length (<tagt>_bytesize_eqn over the lseq clen discriminant),
  and the payload _bytesize_eq.

Verified: LowParse.Spec.IfThenElse; all 64 agentic-tls TLS13.Wire.Generated.*
modules (incl. ServerHello_body, whose serverHello_body_bytesize_eqn_* now prove
on the first try); the agentic-tls main tree; and the QuackyDucky unit harness
(no regression).

entries.subject: QuackyDucky -pulse: mark struct/select high types and synth/tag coercions noextract
entries.message:
QuackyDucky -pulse: mark struct/select high types and synth/tag coercions noextract

Commit bd6ead9e marked variable-length-list spec types (<n>/<n>') and their
synth coercions noextract under -pulse, eliminating per-field F* cons-lists from
the extracted parser C.  But that fix did not cover two other emitters whose
high-level types carry byte (Seq.seq uint8) fields:

  * compile_struct: the high record [type <n> = {...}], its tuple [type <n>'],
    and [synth_<n>]/[synth_<n>_recip] coercions.
  * compile_select (sum/dsum): the high sum [type <n> = | <C>_<case> of ...],
    its [tag_of_<n>] discriminator, and (for implicit selects) the
    parameterised refinement [type <n> (k:...)].

Under -pulse the executable representation is the Vec-based copyful lowtype
([<n>_lowtype]/[<n>_low] with [<n>_vmatch]/[<n>_conv]); the copyful/validate/
jump/writer combinators take the synth coercions as GTot, and the LowParse sum
machinery is normalised into the lowtype-based path that dispatches on
[<n>_tag_of_low] (the LOW tag), never the high [tag_of_<n>].  So these high
types and coercions are reachable only from ghost/noextract spec code, yet
KaRaMeL still materialised them -- lowering an opaque [Seq.seq uint8] field to
the generic [Prims_list__uint8_t] cons-list in the extracted C (e.g. the
[signature = x.snd] in CertificateVerify, and ServerName's [tag_of_serverName]
/ [uu___is_Name_host_name] discriminators) even though no runtime value is ever
built from them.

Emit these definitions noextract under -pulse (gated on emit_pulse); the LowStar
(non-pulse) path uses the record/sum as its actual runtime representation, so
they must stay extractable there.  noextract does not affect F* verification --
only extraction.

Verified by re-extracting the agentic-tls TLS wire parsers (0 KaRaMeL errors):
all .c-body cons-list materialisations disappear (total Prims_list mentions
92 -> 37); the residual Prims_list__uint8_t are pure typedef aliases of
LowParse.Bytes.bytes referenced only in noextract/GTot type signatures and never
instantiated (no KRML_HOST_MALLOC / cons construction builds a list), the
runtime byte path being LowParse_PulseParse_Bytes_lvec_uint8_t (Vec+length).

entries.subject: PulseParse.Bytes: add l2r_safe_writer/size_bounded_vlgenbytes
entries.message:
PulseParse.Bytes: add l2r_safe_writer/size_bounded_vlgenbytes

Graceful left-to-right safe writer and size-computation combinators for a
variable-length byte array framed by a generic (variable-width, e.g. bcvli)
length header (serialize_bounded_vlgenbytes). Mirrors the fixed-width
l2r_safe_writer_bounded_vlbytes' template with the variable-width header
orchestration of l2r_safe_writer_bounded_vlgen_payload: read the payload byte
length n = lvec_len (the header value), fail gracefully when n is out of
[vmin,vmax] (vlbytes_conv None), write the header via the supplied l2r_leaf_writer
hw with width hsize n32, then copy the raw payload bytes; room is checked
incrementally (header then payload) so no SZ.t overflow is possible. Adds a
private helper lemma serialize_bounded_vlgenbytes_bytes_eq deriving the
serialization equation (header ++ raw bytes) from serialize_bounded_vlgen_unfold
+ serialize_synth_eq. The size combinator uses size_add_checked for graceful
overflow. No admits/assumes; module verifies EXIT=0.

entries.subject: 3d: add --use_error_handler_macro option
entries.message:
3d: add --use_error_handler_macro option

Add a new `--use_error_handler_macro` 3D CLI option (default off).
When set, the generated F* and C code uses a C macro
`EVERPARSE_ERROR_HANDLER_MACRO` (from a user-supplied header,
typically wired via --add_include) for error reporting, instead of
the dynamic error-handler callback parameter that is normally threaded
through every validator.

Implementation:

* EverParse3d.Actions.Base.fst{i}, Actions.All.fsti, Interpreter.fst:
  thread a `use_error_handler:bool` parameter through the prelude.
  The error-handler field is typed
  `if use_error_handler then error_handler else unit`, and
  combinators dispatch at runtime to either the dynamic handler or
  the `[@@CMacro] assume val error_handler_macro: error_handler`.

* InterpreterTarget.fst: the 3D frontend emits a literal `true`/`false`
  for the bool when generating F* code, so KaRaMeL specialises and
  C extraction drops the unused handler argument entirely. The literal
  is the negation of `Options.get_use_error_handler_macro ()`.

* Target.fst: when the option is set, the generated C wrapper omits
  the static `DefaultErrorHandler` and the `&DefaultErrorHandler`
  argument from the validator call, to match the dropped parameter.

entries.subject: 3d: make Z3TestGen respect --use_error_handler_macro
entries.message:
3d: make Z3TestGen respect --use_error_handler_macro

The z3 test-case generator (Z3TestGen.fst) hand-writes a C test harness
(testcases.c) that calls the generated validators. It unconditionally
defined a `TestErrorHandler` callback and passed `&TestErrorHandler` as
an argument to every validator call. Under `--use_error_handler_macro`,
however, the generated validators drop the `EVERPARSE_ERROR_HANDLER`
parameter (they invoke the `EVERPARSE_ERROR_HANDLER_MACRO` C macro
directly), so the harness failed to compile with "too many arguments to
function".

Make the harness respect the option, across all three generation modes
(--z3_test, --z3_diff_test, --test_checker):

- Omit the `&TestErrorHandler` argument from validator calls in macro
  mode (keeping the `&context` / Ctxt argument), via a shared
  `test_error_handler_call_arg` helper, in both the witness-call printer
  and the standalone test-checker's mmap main.
- Split the harness preamble so the `TestErrorHandler` definition is
  emitted only in dynamic mode (otherwise it would be an unused
  function), while the always-needed `witness_layer_t` typedef is kept.

The harness verdict (ACCEPTED/REJECTED) is derived from the validator's
return value, so it is unaffected; in macro mode the per-witness error
diagnostics are produced by the user-provided
EVERPARSE_ERROR_HANDLER_MACRO instead of TestErrorHandler. Dynamic-mode
output is unchanged.

The accessor_dsum_tag function is blocked by F*'s (x <: data_t)

facts (parse succeeds, consumed == length, parsed_tag value) but

depend on the coercion.

entries.subject: QD/LowParse: make if-then-else C-extraction monomorphization-friendly
entries.message:
QD/LowParse: make if-then-else C-extraction monomorphization-friendly

The QuackyDucky if-then-else (select) compiler emitted the discriminant tag
constant <n>_cst as a public, extracted top-level let:

  let <n>_cst : <tag> = Seq.seq_of_list [b0; ...; b_{clen-1}]

For a large tag (e.g. the 32-byte ServerHello HelloRetryRequest random magic),
F* lowers this Seq.seq into a nested singleton-buffer cons-list:
  newbuf { hd=b0; tl = newbuf { hd=b1; tl = ... } }   (clen deep)
KaRaMeL's checker (Checker.check', EBufCreate case) re-checks every buffer
initializer TWICE (check_or_infer then check), so the nested initializers are
traversed O(2^clen) times -> C-extraction hangs (>8 min, 100% CPU) on the
post-monomorphization Checker phase. (KaRaMeL itself is treated as fixed.)

<n>_cst is a pure SPEC value: at run time the tag comparison is done
byte-by-byte by <n>_get_byte + LPITE.seqbytes_eq_test, never by reading
<n>_cst, and <n>_cond / <n>_synth are only used by the (erased) spec-level
parse_<n>_param / <n>_vmatch / <n>_conv. Marking <n>_cst, <n>_cond and
<n>_synth 'noextract' keeps them fully available for F* verification while
removing the giant constant from the extracted .krml, so KaRaMeL never sees
it. All three must be noextract together so the extracted code never refers
back to the (now non-extracted) <n>_cst.

The LowParse Pulse if-then-else library is unchanged. No F* verification,
no generated parser/validator/reader/writer signatures change (only the
noextract keyword is added to the three spec-only definitions).

(cherry picked from commit 73f21628825b98f273dd783de85106acea49cd69)

entries.subject: qd -pulse: eta-expand low-level alias defs + test enum/vector/struct aliases
entries.message:
qd -pulse: eta-expand low-level alias defs + test enum/vector/struct aliases

The prior commit removed C function-pointer variables from the *copyful*
alias definitions, but the type-alias code path (single-field structs,
simplified to aliases) also emits low-level Pulse definitions
  let <n>_validator  = <ty>_validator
  let <n>_jumper     = <ty>_jumper
  let <n>_reader     = <ty>_reader
  let <n>_writer     = <ty>_writer
  let <n>_leaf_size  = <ty>_leaf_size
as bare aliases. Whenever the aliased type needs a validator/jumper/leaf
reader (i.e. it is not a constant-size total type), each of these bare
aliases extracts to a C function-pointer *global variable*
(`ret (*f)(args) = g;`).

The existing test corpus never exercised this: the only alias (t10) wraps
the constant-size total type t3, whose validator/jumper are transparent
`.fsti` combinator applications and whose leaf reader/writer/size are not
emitted at all, so no bare low-level alias was ever generated.

Add three single-field-struct aliases that DO hit this path and confirm
they produced function pointers before the fix:
  - t62 = alias of enum `tag`  -> validator + reader + writer + leaf_size
  - t63 = alias of vector `t5` -> validator + jumper
  - t64 = alias of struct `t8` -> validator + jumper
(8 function-pointer variables total in T62.c/T63.c/T64.c).

Fix: fully eta-expand these five pulse-channel (`wp`) alias definitions,
binding and re-passing every argument including the ghost implicits, using
each low-level type's binder structure (validator/jumper/leaf_reader/
l2r_leaf_writer are `stt`; leaf_size is a pure `x -> Pure SZ.t`):
  validator : fun input poffset #offset #pm #v -> g input poffset #offset #pm #v
  jumper    : fun input offset #pm #v -> g input offset #pm #v
  reader    : fun input #pm #v -> g input #pm #v
  writer    : fun x out offset #v -> g x out offset #v
  leaf_size : fun x -> g x

Only the `wp` (pulse) alias lines change; the `wl` (Low*/non-pulse)
versions are untouched, so `qd` (without `-pulse`) output is byte-identical
(verified: 154 files, empty diff). `make -j16 -k quackyducky-pulse-test`
passes and the extracted C now contains zero function-pointer variables.

Two definitions in EverParse3d.State are now opaque to SMT:

- state_dict_weaken_prop: every occurrence otherwise expanded into three
  nested quantifiers, which the promiscuous pattern of state_dict_weaken_prod
  then asserted for every product term in a generated module.
- state_dict_prod: its state_values field is an if, so an SMT encoding that
  unfolds it has to case-split to encode the types of the values of a nested
  product, which is exponential in the nesting depth.

Client modules now reason through characterization lemmas instead. Added
state_dict_weaken_empty, and projector-shaped companions of state_p_empty,
state_p_singleton and state_p_prod, since the disjointness precondition of
state_dict_prod is phrased with the record projector rather than state_p.

Generated code that previously exhausted a 900s budget (and 15GB of memory)
now checks in seconds.

Also point the 3d driver at lib/everparse/3d, src/lowparse/pulse and the
Pulse library when --pulse is given, instead of src/3d/prelude.

entries.subject: rust: drop const_assert!(usize::BITS >= 64) from the CBOR/COSE/CDDL harnesses
entries.message:
rust: drop const_assert!(usize::BITS >= 64) from the CBOR/COSE/CDDL harnesses

The generated Rust no longer assumes a 64-bit usize: every u64->usize
widening is now either runtime-guarded by the portable base-2^15 size
check (sizet_fits_u64 / u64_lte_sizet, which reject oversized lengths
gracefully) or bounded by an actual in-memory slice length (so it cannot
exceed usize::MAX on any target). The proofs rest only on
FStar.SizeT.fits_at_least_16, and Rust guarantees usize is at least
16 bits (Reference [type.numeric.int.size.minimum]), so the code is sound
on any Rust target and the >= 64 assertion is obsolete.

Remove the four const_assert!(usize::BITS >= 64) and the now-unused
static_assertions dependency from each crate (cborrs, cborrs-nondet,
evercosign, cborrs-test). Cargo.lock format versions are left untouched
(det/cose v3, nondet/cddl v4). All four crates build; cose tests pass.

entries.subject: 3d/pulse: make copy buffers an opaque handle, as in Low*
entries.message:
3d/pulse: make copy buffers an opaque handle, as in Low*

Replaces the reference-to-descriptor indirection with the Low* shape: an
abstract copy_buffer_t plus assumed projections that the client implements
in C.  The earlier objection to this -- that pure projections cannot express
a repointing probe -- was wrong: the pre and post of a probe differ in the
stream contents, so a probe does change the slprop.  What had actually
broken was purely a C-level problem, namely that EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T was
a by-value struct that a callee could not repoint.  An opaque void* handle
can be repointed, and EverParseStreamOf then returns the new pointer, which
is exactly how the Low* backend behaves.

The copy_buffer class loses descr_t, descr and the existential in pts_to,
keeping only base_of/len_of/pos_of and reset.  The buffer backend assumes
the type and the three projections, named so that the EverParse bundle
renames them to EverParseStreamOf, EverParseStreamLen and EverParseStreamPos.
The first two are the Low* hooks verbatim, modulo EverParseStreamLen
returning size_t since Pulse stream lengths are SZ.t; the third has no Low*
counterpart and returns the position cell, which Low* validators instead
take as an argument.

Consequently EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T is void* again, straight from
EverParseEndianness.h, so EverParsePulseEndianness.h no longer redefines it
-- which removes the include-order conflict that had forced six hand-written
test stream headers to change includes.  It does republish the three
prototypes, because KaRaMeL emits them into internal/EverParse.h rather than
the public header, and without them a client's definitions would not be
signature-checked.  Target and Z3TestGen drop their --pulse special cases
for probes, and probe_then_validate and the ProbeActions error handler lose
their reference bookkeeping.

Client C code is now source-compatible with Low* apart from adding
EverParseStreamPos and widening EverParseStreamLen to size_t; the probe and
specialize test clients are updated accordingly.

Merge existential preconditions with loop invariant relationships

Combine the two separate existential blocks in Lemma9-13 into a
single existential that tracks the relationships between loop-entry
state and current state at each call site:

- v_old_iter = map_of_list_cons key_eq gk gv v (from next)
- min = update_min(min_old, gk, gv)
- max = update_max(max_old, gk, gv)

For error paths (Lemma9-11, 13): em, count, m, size are unchanged
from loop entry, so the invariant uses them directly. Only vout_old,
min_old, max_old remain existentially quantified.

entries.subject: 3d: reject non-aligned types used in the fields of an aligned type
entries.message:
3d: reject non-aligned types used in the fields of an aligned type

A type with an `aligned` qualifier is laid out by 3d following the C
struct layout rules, and that layout is checked against the C compiler's
own layout by the generated AutoStaticAssertions.c. This is only sound
if every struct or casetype embedded by value in its fields is itself
`aligned`: otherwise 3d lays the embedded type out packed while the C
compiler pads it, and 3d silently emits an AutoStaticAssertions.c that
rightfully fails to compile, which is confusing for the user.

Report this in the frontend instead, in the typesizes pass, where the
`aligned` qualifier is already interpreted. Base types, enums and type
abbreviations of those are unaffected, as are pointer fields.

Add FAILAlignedUsesUnaligned.3d to illustrate the case, and document the
rule in doc/3d-lang.rst.

entries.subject: 3d: name the raw validator answer positionAfter<Field>OrError
entries.message:
3d: name the raw validator answer positionAfter<Field>OrError

For each field, `validate_with_error_handler` binds the validator's raw
answer (a position on success, an error code otherwise) and its caller
binds the very same value once the error handler has run.  Both were
renamed to `positionAfter<Field>`, so KaRaMeL had to disambiguate them
with a numeric suffix, yielding `positionAfterX` / `positionAfterX0` in
every generated validator.  KaRaMeL cannot merge the two bindings
because the error handler's `if` sits in between.

Name the inner one `positionAfter<Field>OrError` instead.  The outer one
keeps the clean name, since that is the value threaded into all the
subsequent fields and hence the one that appears most often.

Measured on src/3d/tests/out.batch-interpret (2052 locals, sibling check
scoped per C function): `positionAfter` disambiguation drops from 208 to
24, and the overall count of numerically disambiguated locals from 327
(16%) to 143 (7%).

Add LowParse.PulseParse.* combinators for non-injective parsers

Define parsing combinators that use pts_to_parsed (parser-only) instead of
pts_to_serialized (which requires a serializer and parser injectivity).

PulseParse.Base (extended):
- leaf_reader/reader types using pts_to_parsed
- leaf_reader_of_reader, reader_of_leaf_reader conversions
- leaf_reader_of_serialized, reader_of_serialized bridges
- read_parsed_from_validator_success (requires ParserStrong)
- ifthenelse_reader, reader_ext utilities

PulseParse.Combinators (new):
- Ghost lemmas: pts_to_parsed_synth_{intro,elim,trade,l2r,r2l,l2r_trade}
- Ghost lemmas: pts_to_parsed_filter_{intro,elim,elim_trade}
- Read: read_synth, read_synth', read_filter with helper types
- Validate: validate_filter, validate_filter', validate_dtuple2
- Jump: jump_dtuple2
- Ret/empty: leaf_read_ret, read_ret, leaf_read_empty, read_empty

PulseParse.BitSum (new):
- read_bitsum' (composition of read_filter and read_synth)

PulseParse.VCList (new):
- Ghost: pts_to_parsed_nlist_1_{intro,elim}, pts_to_parsed_nlist_ext
- Split: nlist_hd_tl, nlist_hd, nlist_tl
- Note: sub-slices have half permission (pm /. 2.0R) due to
  non-injective pts_to_parsed_intro

PulseParse.Recursive (new, stub):
- All Recursive combinators require serialize_recursive_param and cannot
  be ported without a complete redesign of the recursive infrastructure.

Combinators that cannot be rewritten without serializers:
- Writers (l2r_write_*, l2r_leaf_writer): write serialized bytes
- Size (compute_remaining_size): compute serialized byte lengths
- Copy/Gather: need serializer injectivity
- zero_copy_parse: returns trade to pts_to_serialized
- peek_trade_gen/validate_filter_gen: need serializer for sub-slice creation
- split_dtuple2/nondep_then (Combinators): tied to serializer byte sequences
- read_dtuple2: depends on split_dtuple2
- All Recursive operations: inseparable from serialize_recursive_param

Technical notes:
- pts_to_parsed_synth_{elim,l2r,r2l,l2r_trade} require synth_injective f
  (stronger than the Pulse counterparts) because without known bytes we
  need injectivity to recover the pre-image from parse_synth results
- read_parsed_from_validator_success requires ParserStrong to use
  parse_strong_prefix for sub-slice correctness
- VCList nlist_hd_tl produces sub-slices at pm /. 2.0R because
  pts_to_parsed_intro for non-injective parsers halves permission

Skipped modules:
- LowParse.Pulse.Int (per user request)
- LowParse.Pulse.Endianness (no serializer usage)
- LowParse.Pulse.SeqBytes (all operations write serialized data)

lowparse/pulse: l2r_safe_writer_bounded_vlbytes('/) (Phase-1 bytes writers)

Copyful safe serializers for bounded variable-length byte arrays. Write
the l-byte big-endian length header (via mk_n_to_be EI.uint32 l) into
out[0,l) then copy the payload into [l,l+n). Fail gracefully (err=true)

spec nats min/max/l for runtime comparisons. Adds supporting lemmas

entries.subject: 3d --pulse: use EverParse's own Makefile.basic instead of KaRaMeL's
entries.message:
3d --pulse: use EverParse's own Makefile.basic instead of KaRaMeL's

The C generated by `3d --pulse` is self-contained: the Pulse runtime is
bundled into EverParse.c/EverParse.h, and nothing refers to krmllib. But
KaRaMeL's misc/Makefile.basic unconditionally puts krmllib's headers on the
include path and links every executable against libkrmllib.a, which a KaRaMeL
built with LOWSTAR=false does not even produce -- so linking the z3 test-case
generation harness failed.

Rather than patch KaRaMeL, ship our own:

- share/everparse/3d/Makefile.basic, a standalone variant with no krmllib
  dependency. Since it is used without a Makefile.include, it discovers the
  generated C files with a wildcard over the output directory.
- Under --pulse, invoke KaRaMeL with -skip-makefiles unconditionally, so
  neither Makefile.basic nor Makefile.include is emitted (making
  --skip_c_makefiles a no-op as far as KaRaMeL is concerned), and drive the
  C build through EverParse's copy instead, both from 3d.exe itself
  (build_test_exe) and from the --pulse test Makefiles.
- Install it in the binary package alongside the rest of the Pulse runtime.

LowParse.Low.DepLen. This goes in LowParse.Pulse (not PulseParse)
because parse_deplen requires a serializer in its type definition.

entries.message:
Port validate_list_up_to to PulseParse

Create LowParse.PulseParse.ListUpTo.fst with validate_list_up_to ported
from LowParse.Low.ListUpTo to Pulse.

Uses a while loop that iterates: validate one element, read it via
read_parsed_from_validator_success, check the termination condition. If
cond is true, stop with success. If cond is false, advance and continue.
If element validation fails, stop with failure.

Loop invariant tracks consumed bytes: relates parse result at the
initial offset to parse result at the current offset, ensuring the
total consumed bytes are consistent across iterations.

entries.subject: Remove fits_u64 assumption from EverCDDL-generated F* code
entries.message:
Remove fits_u64 assumption from EverCDDL-generated F* code

CDDL.Tool.Gen emitted `assume (SZ.fits_u64)` into every generated .fst,
discharging a SZ.fits_u64 precondition threaded through the
CDDL.Pulse.AST.{Validate,Bundle,Parse} combinator API. That threading
existed solely to convert the `.size` control bounds (WfTStrSize lo/hi)
to size_t at validation (Validate.fst, the sole consumer).

Instead of assuming size_t >= 64 bits, convert the bounds to U64.t (always
valid since hi < 2^64) and compare against the runtime size_t string length
with the portable base-2^15 helpers (u64_lte_sizet / sizet_lte_u64),
matching the already-U64-based serializer side (bundle_str_size). This keeps
`.size` bounds at < 2^64 and is sound on any platform with >= 16-bit size_t
(on a 32-bit target len <= hi is correctly true when hi > 2^32, and lo <= len
correctly false when lo > 2^32).

- CDDL.Pulse.Misc: impl_str_size takes lo hi : U64.t, compares via base-2^15
- CDDL.Pulse.AST.Validate: WfTStrSize uses U64.uint_to_t; drop dead sz_uint_to_t
  and the SZ.fits_u64 conjuncts from the 5 wf refinements
- CDDL.Pulse.AST.Bundle/Parse: drop the now-vestigial SZ.fits_u64 refinements
- CDDL.Tool.Gen: remove the generated preamble assume

Generated COSE + cddl test code now verifies with zero fits_u64 assumptions.

entries.subject: Weaken the field-pointer setter into the enclosing state dictionary
entries.message:
Weaken the field-pointer setter into the enclosing state dictionary

Action_field_ptr_after_with_setter was indexed by the ambient state_dict d
and took its `write_to` callback at that same d. But the setter of an
`output` type runs at that type's own dictionary, so unifying the two
pinned the whole enclosing Action_seq to the output state. A sibling action
on an unrelated mutable parameter then could not discharge its weakening
obligation:

  Subtyping check failed; expected type
    squash (state_dict_weaken_prop (state_dict_singleton k__p (pts_to p))
                                   output_state)

Give the setter the same treatment external actions already get: take the
callee dictionary d' as an argument and weaken into d at construction, via
a mk_field_ptr_after_with_setter helper mirroring mk_action_binding. The
result is stored with Action_call, which is what keeps atomic_action in
universe 1 -- a state_dict field on the constructor would have raised it.

The setter form of field_ptr_after had no test in either backend, which is
how this survived; add one to the static test, where field_ptr_after is
already exercised. It pairs an assignment to a mutable parameter with a
setter write in a single on-success block, which is precisely the
configuration that failed. The client gains a definition of
EverParseNullPtr, declared by the generated EverParse.h next to the other
hooks this backend expects the client to supply and needed only on the
setter path, and the generated Test_OutputTypes.o is added to the link (the
generated makefile emits a rule for it but omits it from
EVERPARSE_ALL_O_FILES).

Verified: the repro fails to verify before and generates correct C after,
with the assignment and the setter call both present; the static test binary
builds and runs; and the bare-statement form of the same construct fails
identically on Low*, so that limitation is pre-existing and unrelated.
make -j16 3d-pulse-test passes (exit 0).

entries.subject: pulse-diff: also compare the sub-directory 3D tests
entries.message:
pulse-diff: also compare the sub-directory 3D tests

The harness only covered the 25 .3d files in src/3d/tests itself. The
sub-directories exercise everything the top-level batch does not:
multi-module compilation, output types, external typedefs and iterators,
conditional compilation, specialization, probes and the error-handler
macro. share/everparse/tests/3d already mirrors the whole tree, so each
has a Pulse counterpart built from the same grammar and there is a pair
to compare.

run_subdir.sh compares one such pair. Rather than carry a table of
per-test build recipes, it works out what to link: everything the
backend generated, minus any file carrying its own main (Z3TestGen's
testcases.c), plus whatever the test supplies by hand -- external-typedef
implementations and the like -- minus its own main and error callbacks,
which the generated driver provides instead. One relative path names the
directory in both trees; an optional `lo=pu` form covers the single
layout that diverges, where Low* emits all the output_types tests into
one interpret.out and Pulse gives each its own directory.

Three supporting changes:

- gen_diff.py handles the out-parameter shapes the sub-directories use:
  BOOLEAN*, and out-parameters of types the test defines itself, such as
  an output type or iter's OUT_T. Those are handed over zeroed, as a
  well-behaved client would, and compared byte for byte -- not poisoned
  with a fill pattern, because some hold pointers the test's own external
  API dereferences. It also recognises and skips the extern/static ABI,
  which takes an opaque stream only the client can construct.

- harness.c gains ProbeAndReadU64 and ProbeInPlace, needed by the probe
  and tagged-union-array tests.

- hx_bytes renders an opaque out-parameter for the trace.

20 configurations now compare clean, covering 34 further entrypoints.
Left out, and documented: extern/static/funptr (opaque input stream),
exttype and goto_return (generation-only, no validator is built), and
output_types/ExternVector.out (its Push() lives in a file that also
carries a main and an error callback).

entries.subject: 3d: get the Low*/Pulse differential test onto the accepting path
entries.message:
3d: get the Low*/Pulse differential test onto the accepting path

Comparing the two backends on inputs they both reject is worth much less than
comparing them on inputs they accept: a rejection exercises one refinement and
stops, while an accepted parse runs the whole validator. Ten of the 49
entrypoints were never once satisfied, and several sub-directory tests were
barely satisfied either, so for those the test was only ever evidence about
the rejecting path. Three separate causes, none of them visible from the
outside:

- CB_LEN was 64, but specialize_test's B64 is 80 bytes, so
  ProbeAndCopy(length=sizeof(B)) could not succeed for any input at all.
- The probe pointer chain was written only into the first 128 bytes of the
  source region, so it was exhausted after one hop and any grammar that
  dereferences deeper always landed in noise. It is now replicated in every
  page.
- Out-parameters were seeded with a fixed poison value. A `mutable` 3D
  parameter is an in/out accumulator the grammar may read, so ActAndCheck's
  `C`, which validates only when the accumulator ends at 0 while its action
  can only increase it, was unsatisfiable by construction. They are now taken
  from the fuzzer-controlled arguments, indexed from the top of the array so
  that adding one does not renumber the scalar arguments, and their seed is
  reported alongside their final value.

Then four ways to reach grammars a blind mutator will not:

- A constant dictionary per entrypoint, collected from the literals of its
  .3d, planted at random offsets in each width and byte order. The literals
  come from the .3d because the interpreter backend compiles them away: ELF's
  magic survives in neither ELF.c nor ELF.fst. They are kept in order of first
  appearance, so a run of the dictionary reproduces a multi-byte magic number
  verbatim, and the corpus is seeded with several such runs.
- A checked-in seed corpus of inputs that EverParse's own `3d --z3_test`
  proved are accepted, for grammars no search can reach -- Arithmetic's
  `_Check` is thirteen consecutive UINT32s each pinned to a value computed
  from earlier fields. seeds.inc is generated by gen_seeds.py and committed,
  so building and running this test still needs neither Z3 nor the generator.
- Seeds in four content families rather than only a byte ramp. All zeroes
  matters most: an empty [:zeroterm] array is two zero bytes and a zero tag
  selects a union's smallest case.
- Budget where it is needed: an entrypoint that has not yet accepted anything
  fuzzes for twenty times the normal iteration count, and a slice of the
  corpus is reserved so that one rare accepted case is not evicted by the
  thousands of distinct ways to fail.

46 of 49 entrypoints now reach their accepting path, against 39 before, and
the sub-directory tests gain a great deal of evidence as well (ifdefs 188 ->
1348 cases, modules 50 -> 276, use_error_handler_macro 36 -> 268). The three
that remain are named in the fuzz log at the end of every run, so the gap
stays visible instead of having to be rediscovered; README.md says what each
of them needs and why the solver does not get there.

Both backends still agree on every case.

entries.subject: 3d: name the remaining prelude locals after the field they belong to
entries.message:
3d: name the remaining prelude locals after the field they belong to

Several validators in the 3D prelude bound their intermediate results to
fixed names (`res`, `result`, `action_result`, `ok`, `has_failed`) with no
`rename_let` attribute.  After inlining, every field of a struct contributed
another local with the very same name, so KaRaMeL had to disambiguate them
with numeric suffixes (`res`, `res0`, `res1`, ...), which makes the generated
C hard to relate back to the .3d source.

Give each of them a `rename_let` keyed on the capitalized field name:

  res           -> resFor<Field>
  result        -> resultFor<Field>, listResultFor<Field>,
                   finalResultFor<Field>
  action_result -> actionResultFor<Field>
  ok            -> okFor<Field>
  has_failed    -> hasFailedFor<Field>, elementHasFailedFor<Field>

To make the field name available, thread a `name: string` argument through
the combinators that did not have one: `validate_drop`, `validate_drop_true`,
`validate_without_reading`, `validate_dep_pair_with_action`, `validate_list`,
`validate_list'`, `validate_list_body`, `validate_fldata`,
`validate_fldata_consumes_all`, `validate_nlist`, `validate_list_up_to`,
`validate_list_up_to_body` and `validate_string`.  `validate_pair` gains a
`name2` argument so that the second component of a pair is named after its
own field rather than after the first one.  At the interpreter call sites the
name comes from the node's `fn`, or from `typ_fieldnames` for the nodes
(`T_drop`) that carry no field name of their own.

`capitalize` moves from `EverParse3d.Actions.Base` to
`EverParse3d.Actions.Common`, which is the only module visible from both
`Actions.Base` and `ProbeActions` (`Actions.Base` depends on `ProbeActions`),
and which has no interface file, so it can still be delta-unfolded by the
specialization normalizer.

Measured on src/3d/tests: locals carrying a KaRaMeL-generated numeric suffix
drop from 462 to 405 out of 2052, and the fixed-name families
(`res`/`result`/`ok`/`action_result`) drop from 77 suffixed declarations to
16.  The `has_failed` locals that remain are in the `--__specialize` probe
helpers, where the field name is a runtime argument and therefore not a
string literal that `rename_let` can consume.

entries.subject: EverCDDL: add CDDL.Spec.AST.Print roundtrip test infrastructure
entries.message:
EverCDDL: add CDDL.Spec.AST.Print roundtrip test infrastructure

Three parallel-runnable targets under src/cddl/tests/roundtrip/:
  dpe          src/cddl/tests/dpe/dpe.cddl   + src/cddl/tests/dpe/dpe_postlude.cddl
  cose_sign    src/cose/cose-sign.cddl       + src/cddl/spec/postlude.cddl
  cose_encrypt src/cose/cose-encrypt.cddl    + src/cddl/spec/postlude.cddl

Per target:

  1. ocaml/gen_fst/Main.exe (links evercddl.lib) calls
     ParseFromFile.parse_from_files on the .cddl inputs, runs the
     extracted CDDL.Spec.AST.Print.program_to_string on the result,
     and writes:

         module <Mname>
         open CDDL.Spec.AST.Base
         let ast : program = [ ... ]

  2. fstar.exe typechecks <Mname>.fst and extracts it to OCaml.

  3. Check.ml (generic) plus a one-line generated main.ml are linked
     against the freshly-extracted <Mname>.ml and evercddl.lib via
     'fstar.exe --ocamlenv ocamlfind ocamlopt -package evercddl.lib'.
     The resulting check.exe re-runs the parser on the same inputs
     and compares with OCaml polymorphic = against <Mname>.ast. On
     mismatch both sides are dumped as program_to_string output for
     easy textual diff.

Polymorphic = is correct on the extracted AST: lists/sums/products
are trivial, and Prims.int = Zarith.Z.t carries a custom comparator.

Each target writes only inside _output/<T>/, so make -j N is safe
across targets. A clean from-scratch parallel run is ~5s on this host
(most of the time is gen_fst.exe build + linking 21 MB binaries).

Wired into src/cddl/tests/Makefile so make -C src/cddl/tests test
(and therefore make cddl-test) now also runs the roundtrip.

entries.subject: 3d/pulse: don't let user parameters collide with the `d`/`sq` binders
entries.message:
3d/pulse: don't let user parameters collide with the `d`/`sq` binders

Under `--pulse`, `print_td_iface_pulse` and the `.fst` printer emit

    val dtyp_T <user binders> (d: EverParse3d.State.state_dict)
                              (sq: squash (state_dict_weaken_prop ... d))

The `d` and `sq` binders were hard-coded and appended *after* the user's
parameters in the same binder list, so any 3D parameter named `d` or `sq` --
mutable or not -- produced ill-formed F*:

    entrypoint
    typedef struct _R (UINT32 d, UINT32 sq) {
      UINT8 a { a > 0 };
      UINT8 b { b < d && b < sq };
    } R;

    * Error 138: Non-linear patterns are not permitted.
      The variable 'd' appears more than once in this function definition.

With a *mutable* `d` the user's binder is instead shadowed by the
`state_dict` one, and the error surfaces as an unsolvable typeclass
constraint `Pulse.Class.PtsTo.has_pts_to EverParse3d.State.state_dict _`.
The Low* backend has no such binders and accepts all of these grammars.

Rename them to `___d` and `___sq`. `Ast.check_reserved_identifier` rejects
any 3D identifier beginning with `___`, so the collision is now impossible
by construction -- the same convention already used for `___output_state`
and `___UINT32`. Also print `Prims.squash` rather than `squash` at these
two sites, so the weakening binder cannot be shadowed either.

Both sites are `pulse ()`-only; the Low* backend is untouched.

Add `ReservedBinders.3d` to both test corpora (they are deliberately kept
diffable), covering `d`/`sq` as mutable parameters, as plain parameters,
and threaded through a nested type call, which is where the dictionary
weakening proof is actually applied.

entries.subject: 3d/pulse: record why the uint64_t static assertion stays unconditional
entries.message:
3d/pulse: record why the uint64_t static assertion stays unconditional

The comment justified the assertion through the extern wrapper's
size_t -> uint64_t -> size_t round trip of the validation origin, which
invites the conclusion that it could be emitted for extern/static only: those
are the backends whose position is an unbounded cumulative stream offset,
whereas a buffer validator is entered from the wrapper with a uint32_t len
and so never sees a position above 2^32.

That conclusion is wrong. probe_then_validate re-enters the inner validator
over the copy buffer, passing it the same error handler together with
CP.len_of dest, and for the buffer backend len_t is an unrefined
FStar.SizeT.t -- the client's EVERPARSE_COPY_BUFFER_T capacity, not the
wrapper's uint32_t. Inside a probe the buffer backend is therefore exactly as
unbounded as extern/static, and since probes are buffer-only under --pulse it
is precisely the backend that would have been exempted. The failure mode is
worse than truncation: the origin subtraction wraps, so a field offset of 4
is reported as 2^64+4.

Comment only; no generated output changes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

entries.subject: Sync TAtMost.3d into the Pulse test tree, and catch such drift early
entries.message:
Sync TAtMost.3d into the Pulse test tree, and catch such drift early

Merging master brought in "Test #321", which added an Issue321 entrypoint
to src/3d/tests/TAtMost.3d. share/everparse/tests/3d is meant to mirror
that tree, but its copy was not updated, so pulse-diff generated a driver
naming an entrypoint the Pulse backend had never been asked to produce:

  driver.c: undefined reference to `TatMostCheckIssue321'

which broke `make 3d-test`.

Copy the grammar across. The Pulse backend compiles it without complaint,
and the new entrypoint now takes part in the differential test, where it
accepts and rejects exactly the inputs the Low* one does.

The failure was harder to read than it should have been. The method rests
on a single driver being valid against both backends, so the two trees
must agree on every entrypoint signature -- an assumption pulse-diff made
silently and left to the linker to enforce, one missing symbol at a time.
gen_diff.py now takes the Pulse directory as well and compares the two
sets up front, reporting every entrypoint that exists on only one side,
and every signature that differs, before emitting anything.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
